homepage.description: An https URL. It is rendered as a link in a desktop application and published to every client, so other schemes are refused: they are instructions to whatever renders the link rather than homepages.

id.description: The plugin's permanent id, matching the SDK's pattern. It is first-come, permanent, and NEVER RECYCLED — it identifies this plugin in every installed copy on every user's machine, so it cannot be released or reassigned later, even if the plugin is delisted.

name.description: What a human sees in the plugin browser.

listed.description: Always false for a newly claimed id: a plugin appears in the index only once a release of it has been approved, and the first release of a new id always goes to human review.

count.description: How many releases are waiting for review.

code.description: The stable machine-readable code to switch on; the enum is closed

detail.description: An explanation specific to this occurrence

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated for client convenience

title.description: A short, human-readable summary; it does not vary with the occurrence

type.description: A URI reference to the documentation for this error code

artifact_sha256.description: The sha256 you computed for the artifact, as 64 hex characters. It is COMPARED against the hash this server computes from the bytes it downloads, and then discarded — the published hash is always the server's. A mismatch does not publish; it goes to review.

artifact_url.description: An https URL the artifact can be downloaded from. It is transport only: the server downloads it and computes the hash itself. A URL carrying credentials in its userinfo is refused, because this value is published in the index to every client.

minimum_app_version.description: The lowest nParse+ version this release runs on, or null for no constraint. Null and empty are the same statement here and both mean no constraint.

notes.description: Plain-text patch notes for a human to read in the client. Not Markdown and not HTML (ADR-0013); at most 2048 bytes.

sdk_specifier.description: The nParse+ SDK versions this release supports, as a PEP 440 specifier. Carried, not evaluated.

version.description: The release's version. This registry carries it and compares it; the client evaluates version semantics.

artifact_bytes.description: The artifact's size in bytes, counted during the download. Absent when the artifact could not be fetched.

artifact_sha256.description: The sha256 THIS SERVER computed from the bytes it downloaded. This is the value that is published, and it is not necessarily the one you submitted. Absent when the artifact could not be fetched.

quarantine.description: Every rule that sent this release to review. Absent when it went live. A new plugin id is always one of these: the first appearance of an id always gets a human, whatever the submitter's trust level.

replayed.description: True when this idempotency key had been seen before and this is the original result rather than a new submission.

review.description: Why this release is waiting, in a sentence written for a human.

state.description: Where the release is: pending while it waits for a human, approved once it is the plugin's live release. A new plugin id always gets human review, and trust never bypasses that.

superseded_release_id.description: The release this one retired, when it published automatically.

verified.description: Whether this server downloaded the artifact and computed its hash. FALSE MEANS THE BYTES WERE NOT CHECKED: the release is recorded and sent to review, and the review field says why. It is never a success.

artifact_sha256.description: The hash this server computed, when it managed to.

review_note.description: What was recorded on the release.

verified.description: Whether the artifact could be fetched and hashed THIS TIME. False is not an error: the release is still pending and the reason is recorded.

note.description: Why. Optional when approving; REQUIRED when rejecting, because the author cannot see the queue and has no other way to learn what to fix.

superseded_release_id.description: The release this approval retired, when there was one. A listing changing with nothing saying so is indistinguishable from a bug.

level.description: The tier. trusted lets this account's version bumps of an already-approved plugin publish without a human; blocked refuses its publishes outright; new is the default and sends everything to review.

note.description: Why. REQUIRED: a tier with no stated reason is one nobody can review later, and raising somebody to trusted is the decision that most needs to be explainable a year afterwards.

artifact_sha256.description: The hash THIS SERVER computed. Absent when the artifact could not be fetched, and a release with no hash cannot be approved.

artifact_url.description: The URL the artifact was fetched from. Transport only; the hash is the security boundary.

first_release.description: True when this plugin has nothing approved yet, so this submission is the first appearance of the id. That is where impersonation is caught.

review_note.description: Why this is waiting: a hash mismatch, an artifact that could not be fetched, or simply that nothing publishes without a human yet.

verified.description: Whether this server fetched the artifact and hashed it. False means it could not, and the release cannot be approved until a reverify succeeds.

pat.description: A personal access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer nprs_pat_…`, where the prefix is followed by an 8-character public identifier and the secret. A token in a query string is rejected with 401, with no exception: query strings land in access logs, proxy logs and browser history.

session.description: A browser session. It is the only credential that satisfies a capability-floor operation — minting tokens, changing owners, setting trust — because a token that could perform one would be equivalent to the account.

put.description:
Trust governs ONE thing: whether a version bump of an already-approved plugin can publish without a human.

It never governs the first appearance of a plugin id — that always gets a human, whatever the tier — and it never governs who may review, which is configured in the deployment. A tier that did both would let a trusted publisher approve their own submissions.

**It is never raised automatically.** A counter of successful publishes is a counter an attacker can run up: publish four harmless releases, earn the tier, publish the fifth.

PUT rather than POST because a tier is a property of the account, not an event. The history is in the audit log, which nothing can edit.

post.description:
Registers a plugin id to your account and makes you its owner.

**Ids are first-come, permanent and never recycled.** An id identifies this plugin in every installed copy on every user's machine, so it cannot be released or reassigned later — delisting a plugin clears its listing and keeps the claim. Choose carefully.

Claiming does not publish anything. The plugin appears in the index once a release of it has been approved, and **the first release of a new id always goes to human review**, whatever your trust level.

This is session-only: no personal access token can claim an id, however scoped.

Submits a release of a plugin you hold.

**The server downloads the artifact and computes its sha256 itself.** The `artifact_sha256` you send is compared against that value and then discarded; the hash this registry publishes is always one it derived from bytes it read (ADR-0008). If the two disagree, the release is not published: it is recorded and sent to human review, with the mismatch noted.

**An artifact that could not be downloaded is not published either.** It goes to review with the reason recorded and `verified` false. "We could not check" and "we checked and it was fine" never produce the same answer.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. A re-run with the same key returns the original result; the same key with a different body is a 409.

parameters.description: An opaque key identifying this publish attempt. Re-running a workflow with the same key returns the original result instead of submitting a second release; reusing it with a different body is a 409.

Everything submitted and not yet decided, oldest first.

`first_release` marks a submission that is the first appearance of a plugin id. Those always require a human, whatever the submitter's trust level.

`verified` false means this server could not fetch the artifact. Such a release cannot be approved — the database refuses a listing with no hash — so it must be reverified or rejected.

Makes the release the plugin's live one and retires whatever it replaces.

The retired release is not deleted: history is kept, because those rows are the record of what was approved and by whom.

A release whose artifact this server never hashed cannot be approved.

post.description:
Refuses the release. A reason is required: the author cannot see the queue and has no other way to learn what to fix.

The row stays, and so does its claim on the version — a version is used once per plugin, ever, so a rejected 1.0.0 does not free 1.0.0.

post.description:
For a release this server could not verify at publish time — an upstream outage, a slow morning.

It can only ever FILL IN A BLANK. A release that already carries a hash is refused, because a path that could recompute one is a path that could swap the bytes behind a listing without anybody reviewing the swap.

Without this, a thirty-second outage would permanently consume a version number: a version is used once per plugin, ever, so the author's only remedy would be to publish a different one.
